finding.title: _resolve_path in check-freeze.sh fails on missing parent directories and intermediate directory symlinks, allowing dotdot and symlink boundary escapes while falsely denying new subdirectories on macOS
finding.detail: In freeze/bin/check-freeze.sh:169-188, _resolve_path only follows symlinks on the final path component (while [ -L "$_p" ]) and runs cd "$(dirname "$_p")" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P || printf "%s" "$_dir" on the immediate parent directory. Whenever a parent directory does not exist yet (for example, Write or NotebookEdit creating a file in a new subdirectory), cd fails and falls back to the raw uncanonicalized _dir string: (1) <boundary>/../outside/new-dir/secret.ts retains its <boundary>/ prefix and is allowed outside the boundary; (2) <boundary>/out-link/new-dir/secret.ts (where out-link is an in-boundary directory symlink pointing outside) fails both [ -L "$_p" ] and cd, retaining <boundary>/out-link/ and allowing the escape; (3) <boundary>/.. leaves basename as .. and is allowed; and (4) on macOS where /tmp and /var are symlinks to /private/tmp and /private/var, FREEZE_DIR resolves via pwd -P to /private/var/folders/.../boundary while a legitimate new subdirectory write <boundary>/new-subdir/Component.tsx fails cd and stays /var/folders/.../boundary/new-subdir/Component.tsx, falsely denying an in-boundary write.
finding.recommendation: Walk path components left-to-right in _resolve_path (collapsing . and .. and expanding symlinks via readlink at every component depth, bounded to 40 hops) and walk up to the deepest existing ancestor directory before running cd && pwd -P.

finding.title: check-freeze.sh omits tilde expansion on FILE_PATH and uses GNU-only sed /\+ quantifier that fails on macOS BSD sed
finding.detail: In freeze/bin/check-freeze.sh:85-88, FREEZE_DIR expands a leading ~/ or ~ to $HOME, but lines 143-149 omit tilde expansion on FILE_PATH and instead join FILE_PATH onto $(pwd)/. When pwd is inside FREEZE_DIR, an out-of-boundary tilde path like ~/.zshrc becomes $(pwd)/~/.zshrc and is falsely allowed; when pwd is outside FREEZE_DIR, an in-boundary tilde path ~/project/src/index.ts becomes $(pwd)/~/project/src/index.ts and is falsely denied. In addition, line 157 uses sed "s|/\+|/|g;s|/$||", where \+ is a GNU BRE extension that macOS BSD sed treats as a literal plus sign rather than one-or-more slashes: double slashes are not collapsed on macOS, and UNC paths (//server/share/...) receive an extra _FP_LEAD=/ prefix to become ///server/share/..., breaking UNC boundary matching on macOS.
finding.recommendation: Expand leading ~/ and ~ on FILE_PATH before gstack_hook_normalize_path (matching FREEZE_DIR), and replace sed "s|/\+|/|g;s|/$||" with portable POSIX BRE sed "s|//*|/|g;s|/$||".

finding.title: gstack_hook_normalize_path backslash-to-slash replacement could turn a POSIX filename containing literal backslashes into dotdot path traversal
finding.detail: In careful/bin/hook-extract.sh:108-115, gstack_hook_normalize_path executes GSTACK_HOOK_PATH="${GSTACK_HOOK_PATH//\\//}", which if reached on Linux or macOS would rewrite a literal filename like a\..\..\etc\x into a/../../etc/x.
finding.recommendation: Verify whether gstack_hook_normalize_path guards the backslash rewrite behind GSTACK_HOOK_IS_WINDOWS or Windows prefix shapes.
